correctness.rationale: A label 1 would require a positive neighbor and contradict support independence. Every private corona pair must be precisely (3,0), (0,2), or (0,3). The positions of core label 3 form an arbitrary independent set I; a private leaf has label 2 exactly at an arbitrary subset J of N_G(I), since other core vertices are zero and can only be defended by a neighboring core 3 or a private leaf 3. Conversely every such (I,J) is valid, with weight 3n-|J|. Binomial expansion yields the complete polynomial, while extension to maximal independent sets proves max |N_G(I)|=n-i(G); top coefficient counts all minimal weight functions. Independent brute-force checks on 79 base graphs and 8,421,904 full labelings match every coefficient. Finite computations are not used as the arbitrary-order proof.

originality.rationale: The full 2019 initiating primary preprint defines the IDRDF predicate and includes a special corona construction but no all-function polynomial. The materially inspected 2022 Theorem 3 on tree coronas gives an extremal scalar characterization and an independent-domination minimum construction, acknowledged as prior coverage, not a complete feasible-function bijection and invertible weight transform for arbitrary base graphs. A complete outer-independent corona theorem involves the opposite independence requirement, and related indexed generating-function work treats other Roman predicates or graph classes. No equivalent or dominating all-function statement was identified; incomplete page-level access to the 2022 PDF remains a specific documented risk.
residual_risks: The 2022 publisher PDF could not be accessed for complete page-by-page inspection; its central corona Theorem 3 and proof are available through indexed publisher text, but other material could conceivably affect the literature comparison.
A differently phrased or unindexed full independent double Roman corona polynomial might exist.
The independent-set neighborhood enumerator itself is not asserted to be new as a graph invariant or to distinguish all nonisomorphic graphs.

value.rationale: The result provides a bijection that classifies every feasible, including nonoptimal, independent double Roman function on leaf coronas of any base graph. The invertible polynomial identity transfers the entire open-neighborhood distribution of independent sets into a graph-domination weight enumerator and recovers it, thereby giving every coefficient and a nontrivial optimum count. The P4 example has five minimum IDRDFs but only three minimum independent dominating sets, demonstrating information genuinely beyond the previously studied scalar extrema and motivating the exact all-function polynomial.
